agree.reason: A quick-reading committee member gets concrete, uncommon evidence (sole 3 a.m. shift, software-flagged mastitis worth about $8,000, a covered emergency absence), but the garbled sentence "which is good" on written English is the line a doubtful reader stops at.

honest.reason: The core facts are accurate, but some details are mildly embellished beyond the brief: "Nobody else is on the farm at that hour," his responsibility for "anything that goes wrong," and his father becoming "seriously" ill.

works_the_facts.reason: The $8,000 figure is used well, but the letter never turns "two missed shifts in three years" into its stronger form (about 780 scheduled shifts, two missed) and never counts the roughly 25 shifts his cousin covered.

right_comparison.reason: The letter links his work to what the program teaches but gives no comparison to other workers or to typical applicants that would help this one stand out among about 150.

qualification.reason: The written-English caveat names a weakness, a remedy (the night class) and evidence (passing the safety test on the second try), but gives no checkable date or progress measure, and its key sentence is muddled.

objections.reason: The likely objections about reliability (the 5-week absence) and written coursework are each raised and answered with facts, though the botched phrase partly undercuts the answer on English.

fit.reason: It is a one-page letter from the farm manager with a callback number, as the brief asked, though it has no date and only a bare letterhead.
